text:
Marta R: Hi team — customer 'FinServX' hit an outage: when using streaming + tool calls their tool args arrive truncated mid-JSON and we get a JSONDecodeError on the function invocation. They see the model start a tool call but args are incomplete.

Jae Park: Can you paste the exact error and a raw capture of the SSE/chunked stream?

Marta R: Error from our gateway logs: `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 482 (char 481)` (stack trace attached). Raw stream snippet from customer (sanitized):
```
data: {"type":"tool_call","name":"charge_card","arguments":"{\"amount\":100,\"currency\":\"USD\",\"card\":\"tok_\"}

data: {"type":"tool_call","name":"charge_card","arguments":"{\"amount\":100,\"currency\":\"USD\",\"card\":\"tok_abc123\"}"
```
They see the second chunk continuing the args but our function deserializer already tried to parse the partial first chunk.

Liam Chen: Interesting — looks like the middleware tried to parse on per-chunk basis instead of concatenating the event stream. Which client lib are they using?

Marta R: Node fetch + server-sent events polyfill. They are behind a corporate proxy (Akamai) and sometimes HTTP/2 is used.

Oncall-Eng: Is the problem reproducible internally? If we can reproduce we can test whether intermediary splits chunks at N bytes.

Marta R: I reproduced locally by running a tiny Node script to stream the same payload in two writes with a short delay; our runtime attempted to parse each 'data:' event as a full JSON and failed on partial content. Repro steps I used:
```
# repro Node (simplified)
const http = require('http');
http.createServer((req,res)=>{
  res.write('data: {"type":"tool_call","name":"charge","arguments":"{\\"id\\":\\"tok_');
  setTimeout(()=>res.end('abc"}\\n'), 50);
}).listen(4000);
```
Then client receives two chunks and our parse stage emits decode error.

Jae Park: Thanks — that clarifies the flow. Two hypotheses: 1) the runtime's streaming parser treats each SSE 'data' frame independently and attempts immediate JSON parse (bug), or 2) some proxy/transport is splitting a single string between TCP/HTTP frames and we don't properly reassemble before deserializing. Which layer is doing the parse?

Liam Chen: Runtime currently does a streaming parser that attempts to parse complete JSON per incoming buffer using a naive attempt-and-fail pattern. If a parse fails, it logs and drops the event. That's a smell. We should buffer until we detect a complete JSON (balanced braces or a length prefix) before parsing.

Oncall-Eng: For mitigation: ask the customer to disable streaming or switch to non-stream tool-calls for now, and we can push a quick server-side fix to buffer per-event until valid JSON. Also suggest they force HTTP/1.1 (avoid HTTP/2 multiplexing) as a temporary check.

SupportBot: Created support ticket INF-3248 and internal bug RNW-5679 (eng-runtime) — link: https://internal.redwood/bugs/RNW-5679

Marta R: Customer declined full disable; they need streaming. They can try base64-encoding the arguments as a short-term workaround to avoid early-quotes splitting mid-stream. However that's not great UX.

Jae Park: Action items: 1) Eng-runtime to change streaming parser to accumulate until a complete JSON payload is formed (heuristic: count braces, handle escaped quotes) OR switch to newline-delimited JSON with an explicit delimiter. 2) Add a regression test that simulates mid-json chunk splits and proxy-like behavior. 3) Notify support and customer of ETA.

Liam Chen: I'll take RNW-5679. Quick patch outline: maintain a per-stream buffer, append incoming data, attempt incremental parse only when top-level JSON is balanced OR when we hit a configured max latency buffer flush. Fallback: if parse still fails after 500ms, log full buffer and drop with more informative error to caller.

Oncall-Eng: Also add instrumentation to log chunk sizes/headers (Content-Encoding, Transfer-Encoding), and record whether HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 was used — that will help prove proxy splitting involvement.

Marta R: Customer is in US-East and affected intermittently during high traffic times. I told them we'll prioritize and they appreciate a temporary recommendation: switch to synchronous tool call or CDN bypass.

Jae Park: Good. Please post the customer's raw request headers (sanitized) in RNW-5679 and add the repro script. Mark escalation P2.

Marta R: Done. Added headers and a capture from Wireshark showing packet boundary aligning with the split.

Liam Chen: I'll push a small fix and a test tomorrow. If anyone sees similar errors in the logs search for 'JSONDecodeError' plus 'tool_call' and chunk-size patterns.

Marta R: Thanks. I'll follow up with the customer timeline and keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
